# libfuse-abi-fortran: the Fortran participant binding (docs/dev/abi-design.md,
# "Fortran: ffuse"). ffuse.f90 (the module a Fortran program `use`s) and
# fuse_fortran_shim.c (the ffuse_<entry> C functions ffuse.f90's bind(C)
# interfaces reference) are both GENERATED by tools/gen-abi.py from
# include/fuse/abi/entries.def and committed -- edit the .def and re-run
# `python3 tools/gen-abi.py --write`, never these two files directly.
#
# STATIC, deliberately: the shim's only undefined symbol is
# fuse_coupler_abi(), declared in include/fuse/abi/participant.h but DEFINED
# in libfuse-abi (src/abi, the sibling library of this ABI). An archive
# does not need that symbol resolved to be built, only a program that links
# it does -- so this library, and everything that does not itself need
# libfuse-abi (the generator, the module compile, the sizes test, the shim
# compile), builds whether or not libfuse-abi exists yet in this checkout.
#
# BEFORE the first use, not just before install(): a bare ${CMAKE_INSTALL_*}
# reference inside a target_include_directories() genexpr is substituted
# when that command runs, not lazily at install time, so calling this after
# the $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:...> use below silently produced
# $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:/fuse-fortran> (empty variable) -- caught by an
# installed consumer's "includes non-existent path '/fuse-fortran'" error,
# not by the configure of this project itself.
include(GNUInstallDirs)

# ffuse_provider.f90 (the adapter host): the provider
# direction's own Fortran binding -- a Fortran PLUGIN `use`s it to build a
# fuse_provider_abi_v1 table out of its own bind(C) procedures and export
# fuse_provider_abi (docs/dev/abi-design.md, "Provider direction"). It `use`s
# ffuse's own struct declarations (fuse_field_view, fuse_step_request, ...),
# so it is built into the SAME library, in the same compile, as a plain
# `.f90` source list dependency -- gfortran resolves `use ffuse` against the
# .mod ffuse.f90's own compile just emitted into this target's own module
# directory, with no extra wiring needed.
add_library(fuse-abi-fortran STATIC
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/ffuse.f90
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/ffuse_provider.f90
  ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/fuse_fortran_shim.c
)
add_library(fuse::abi-fortran ALIAS fuse-abi-fortran)
# EXPORT_NAME, matching every layer in src/CMakeLists.txt (fuse::base etc.):
# the installed, find_package()'d imported target is fuse::abi-fortran too,
# not fuse::fuse-abi-fortran (install(EXPORT)'s NAMESPACE prefixes the RAW
# target name unless this property renames it).
set_target_properties(fuse-abi-fortran PROPERTIES EXPORT_NAME abi-fortran)

target_include_directories(fuse-abi-fortran PRIVATE
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
)

set(FUSE_ABI_FORTRAN_MODULE_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/mod)
set_target_properties(fuse-abi-fortran PROPERTIES
  Fortran_MODULE_DIRECTORY ${FUSE_ABI_FORTRAN_MODULE_DIR}
  POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON
)
# A consumer `use ffuse`s this directory; test/CMakeLists.txt's Fortran
# registrations read the property back rather than restating the path. The
# INSTALL_INTERFACE half matches the install(DIRECTORY ...) below.
target_include_directories(fuse-abi-fortran INTERFACE
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${FUSE_ABI_FORTRAN_MODULE_DIR}>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}/fuse-fortran>
)

target_compile_options(fuse-abi-fortran PRIVATE
  $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:Fortran>:-std=f2008;-Wall;-Wextra;-Werror;-fimplicit-none>
  # -fvisibility=hidden (abi-design.md: the shim exports ffuse_* only, via the
  # explicit default-visibility attribute on each function in the generated
  # .c file itself) is a C/C++ compiler flag; gfortran does not accept it, so
  # this is restricted to the C source with a generator expression.
  $<$<COMPILE_LANGUAGE:C>:-fvisibility=hidden>
)

# fuse_fortran_shim.c's once-init (pthread_once) needs the threading library;
# find_package(Threads) is the portable way to get -lpthread where that is a
# separate library (Linux) and nothing extra where it is not (macOS/libSystem).
# PRIVATE is enough even though this is a dependency of a STATIC library:
# CMake forwards a static target's PRIVATE link libraries onto the final
# consumer's link line precisely because the archive itself cannot record
# that dependency the way a shared object would.
find_package(Threads REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(fuse-abi-fortran PRIVATE Threads::Threads)

# Installed into the SAME fuse-coupler package src/CMakeLists.txt's own
# install(TARGETS ... EXPORT fuse-coupler-targets) populates (the export set
# name is global to the configure, not tied to which directory calls
# install(TARGETS); this call only needs to run sometime before CMake's
# Generate step, which add_subdirectory(fortran)'s early position in the
# top-level CMakeLists.txt guarantees). fuse/abi/participant.h itself is
# installed already by that file's `install(DIRECTORY include/fuse ...
# PATTERN "*.h")` glob; only the Fortran .mod is this library's to install.
install(TARGETS fuse-abi-fortran
  EXPORT fuse-coupler-targets
  LIBRARY DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}
  ARCHIVE DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}
  RUNTIME DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_BINDIR}
  INCLUDES DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}
)
install(DIRECTORY ${FUSE_ABI_FORTRAN_MODULE_DIR}/
  DESTINATION ${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}/fuse-fortran
  FILES_MATCHING PATTERN "*.mod"
)
